scope: P2 diagnostic of the EGO camera-pose input delivery gap using ROS tracing; no production source or runtime parameters changed.

configuration.qualification: Both are diagnostic settings; neither is frozen for acceptance.

run_43_minimal_trace.harness: Same #37 runtime harness, domain, partition, and world; only run output directory and EGO install overlay changed.

run_44_callback_trace.harness: Same healthy-input harness and patch 0016 overlay; adds callback and executor tracepoints to the minimal publisher/take trace.

timeout_group_sample_delivery.interpretation: This isolated timeout coincided with short input spacing; it did not show a long pose take delay.

callback_and_executor_observations.qualification: The trace does not show a multi-hundred-millisecond callback or executor wait. It does not prove the pose subscription was ready but skipped by the executor, nor reveal the DDS reader's internal availability state.

assessment: In both traces, every mapping-adapter pose/depth RMW publication matched an eventual EGO RMW take by the same middleware source timestamp; this is evidence of delayed consumption rather than a permanent missing sample in these traces.

Pose publication-to-EGO-take delay was repeatedly much larger than depth delay. In #44, 15 and 23 pose messages were taken in a burst after the corresponding timeout groups, with maximum delays of 1.99 s and 2.36 s. The pose writer continued publishing during those groups.
The external probe's wall receipt intervals alone are not treated as publisher timing; #42 showed the probe callback itself can lag. #43/#44 use writer and EGO RMW events for the delivery comparison.

The evidence localizes the symptom to delayed pose consumption inside EGO's subscription path. It does not distinguish DDS reader availability/notification from executor ready-entity selection or another RMW behavior. No multithreaded change was attempted because EGO's input, map timer, and reset paths share unprotected GridMap state.
No PX4 control, arming, actuator, real flight, or scheduled depth-fault window was part of these runs. These are development diagnostics, not P2 acceptance.
limitations: Runs #43 and #44 are single 60 s observations; timeout frequency and latency are not statistically qualified.
Callback tracing can perturb timing. #43 used only five tracepoint classes and reproduced >0.4 s pose take delays, but that does not quantify the perturbation in either run.
RMW tracepoints do not expose Fast DDS sample-rejected counters or prove when a received sample became executable by the ROS executor.
Patch 0016 remains optional diagnostic-only; the 0.4 s timeout and -0.15 m map lower bound remain PROVISIONAL.

A targeted kernel scheduler probe was attempted but unavailable: LTTng kernel tracing is not provided in the build container, and host perf tracepoint access is denied. Process run-queue state is therefore unmeasured.

scheduler_probe_capability.container_lttng_kernel_trace: unavailable: lttng list -k reports "Kernel tracer not available"
scheduler_probe_capability.consequence: No kernel runnable/running-state evidence was collected; RMW/ROS executor traces do not resolve process scheduling versus DDS reader readiness.
